suspicions.claim: The private_email method is added to UserSchema but not to UpdateUserSchema, so PUT /api/me responses may still include the email field for other users when updating their own profile.
suspicions.trigger: Log in as user A, then PUT /api/me with any valid update data; read back the response JSON and check if 'email' field is present (it should be, since it's your own). Then log in as user B, GET /api/users/<A_id> and verify email is absent. The suspicion is that PUT /api/me might leak email in some edge case, but the main issue is that UpdateUserSchema lacks the private_email method.

suspicions.claim: The private_email method uses token_auth.current_user() which may return None in DISABLE_AUTH mode, causing email to be hidden even for the user themselves when authentication is disabled.
suspicions.trigger: Set DISABLE_AUTH=true, restart app, then GET /api/users/1 without authentication; check if 'email' field is present in response (it should be, since user id 1 is assumed).

suspicions.claim: The private_email method compares me.id with data.get('id'), but data may not have 'id' key during serialization of collections (e.g., followers lists), causing email to be incorrectly hidden or shown.
suspicions.trigger: Log in as user A, GET /api/users/<B_id>/followers where B has followers; check if follower objects include 'email' field (they should not, unless the follower is the current user).

suspicions.claim: The private_email method is a @post_dump hook on UserSchema, but PostSchema includes a nested UserSchema for 'author'; this may cause email to be hidden in post author objects even when the post author is the current user.
suspicions.trigger: Log in as user A, create a post, then GET /api/posts/<post_id>; check if author.email is present (it should be, since you are the author).

suspicions.claim: The private_email method may cause email to be missing from the /api/me endpoint response if the user object serialization doesn't include 'id' in data when dumping the current user.
suspicions.trigger: Log in as any user, GET /api/me; verify that 'email' field is present in response (it must be, since it's your own profile).

suspicions.claim: The private_email method uses data.get('id') which returns None if 'id' is missing, causing me.id != None to be True and email to be popped even for the current user in some serialization contexts.
suspicions.trigger: Log in as user A, GET /api/users (list all users); check if your own user object in the list includes 'email' (it should, since it's you).
